papers.title: Tropical QFT and the sine-Gordon model
papers.abstract: A tropical quantum field theory is an exactly solvable deformation limit of an ordinary QFT, governed by a non-linear partial differential equation. We use the integrable two-dimensional sine-Gordon theory as a testbench to compare the exact features of an undeformed model with its tropical counterpart. We classify scale-invariant tropical QFTs in $D=2$ and leverage functional renormalization group methods to demonstrate that all scale-invariant theories with periodic effective actions are infrared fixed points of flows originating from sine-Gordon Lagrangians. For the tropical sine-Gordon model, we compute the $\beta$-functions exactly, solve the renormalized theory both via a convergent expansion and numerically for all admissible couplings, and illustrate the complete renormalization group flow from the Gaussian to the IR fixed point. Finally, we study the large-order behaviour of the loop expansion and relate it to the Hamilton-Jacobi equation, whose solutions we interpret as tropical instantons.

papers.title: Scalene Yang-Baxter triples realize all nearest-neighbour Hamiltonians with global additive symmetries
papers.abstract: We establish that bond Hamiltonian densities, up to local difference terms whose sum vanishes under periodic boundary conditions, lying in the commutant of bond operators, $w_j\pm w_{j+1}$, is a necessary and sufficient condition for a one-dimensional nearest-neighbour Hamiltonian to conserve a uniform or staggered sum of the one-site operators $w_j$. Starting from these local commutants, we show that every such Hamiltonian and its conserved charge can be obtained from monodromy matrices constructed using regular and non-regular members of scalene Yang-Baxter triples. The results hold on periodic chains of length $L\geq3$, with even length required in the staggered case. The results do not require translation invariance, and hence the interaction on each bond can be chosen independently from the full corresponding commutant. Our representation-independent construction applies in arbitrary finite local dimension and exhausts the Hamiltonians with either prescribed additive symmetry, without requiring ordinary Yang-Baxter integrability. We illustrate the construction with spin-$\tfrac12$ and spin-1 systems and discuss its relation to the double-commutant theorem. Classifying the one-site generators $w$ and their associated bond commutants provides a route to classifying such Hamiltonians with additive conserved charges.

papers.title: Modular Properties of Generalised Gibbs Ensembles: The Deformed KdV Hierarchy
papers.abstract: We construct a set of conserved charges which are deformations of quantum KdV charges. They are associated with the modular transformation of a GGE with the spin-$\sigma$ KdV charge inserted with chemical potential $\alpha_\sigma$. The charges are formal power series in the chemical potential, with coefficients given by local integrals of motion. We define local recursion relations and equivalent flow equations, prove commutativity to all orders, and establish uniqueness of the currents modulo total derivatives for a fixed generating series. We show that the eigenvalues of these deformed charges can be obtained from the thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz in two models. In the $c=1/2$ free fermion theory, the deformed charges reduce to explicit linear combinations of undeformed KdV charges, and their ground-state eigenvalues agree with the TBA expansion to all orders. In the Lee-Yang model, we find numerical agreement through cubic order in the spin-$5$ deformation for the first few charges evaluated on low-lying states.

papers.title: Proof of a Universal Speed Limit on Fast Scrambling in Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: We prove that the time required for sustained information scrambling in any Hamiltonian quantum system is universally at least logarithmic in the entanglement entropy of scrambled states. This addresses two foundational problems in nonequilibrium quantum dynamics. (1) It sets the earliest possible time for the applicability of equilibrium statistical mechanics in a quantum system coupled to a bath at a finite temperature. (2) It proves a version of the fast scrambling conjecture, originally motivated in models associated with black holes, as a fundamental property of quantum mechanics itself. Our result builds on a refinement of the energy-time uncertainty principle in terms of the infinite temperature spectral form factor in quantum chaos. We generalize this formulation to arbitrary initial states of the bath, including finite temperature states, by mapping Hamiltonian dynamics with any initial state to nonunitary dynamics at infinite temperature. A regularized spectral form factor emerges naturally from this procedure, whose decay is universally constrained by analyticity in complex time. This establishes an exact speed limit on information scrambling by the most general quantum mechanical Hamiltonian, without any restrictions on locality or the nature of interactions.

papers.title: Bulk OPE Coefficients of the $E$-Series Virasoro Minimal Models
papers.abstract: We present bulk-primary operator-product coefficients for every Virasoro minimal model with an $E_6$, $E_7$, or $E_8$ modular invariant. Dividing by a universal product of chiral generalized-minimal-model OPE coefficients reduces the conformal bootstrap problem to a finite algebraic problem governed by root-of-unity quantum-group $6j$ symbols. The exceptional factors of the OPE coefficients can be chosen independent of the second Kac indices $s$, and their dependence on the central charge reduces to finitely many reference cases and explicit phases. A finite computer-assisted calculation yields candidate algebraic $s=1$ seed data and high-precision numerical evidence for existence and uniqueness modulo primary-field signs. We prove that exact existence and uniqueness for these seeds imply the corresponding result for all Kac labels within the genus-zero bulk locality and crossing equations; the finite seed step remains uncertified. The three families require $18$, $32$, and $107$ representative reduced OPE coefficients for $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$, respectively. We provide reconstruction conventions and coefficient tables for both unitary and nonunitary models. Our calculation assumes only Virasoro symmetry, bulk locality (permutation symmetry) and OPE associativity (crossing equations).

papers.title: Graph-theoretic framework for semi-Markov networks: transient and stationary occupation probabilities, hitting times and weak ergodicity breaking
papers.abstract: Semi-Markov networks provide a natural framework for describing stochastic transitions between coarse-grained states with non-exponential dwell times, with applications ranging from biophysics and neuroscience to epidemiology and finance. Here, it is shown that finite semi-Markov networks admit explicit combinatorial representations of their Laplace-transformed occupation probabilities and hitting-time distributions as sums over weighted spanning trees and forests of an augmented graph. These representations yield asymptotic results, including a generalization of the Markov Chain Tree Theorem to semi-Markov networks, in which the rate constants replaced by pseudo-rates given by the inverse mean sojourn time weighted by the exit probability through this channel, as well as the long-time scaling of hitting-time survival probabilities in the presence of infinite-mean sojourn times. They also extend recently derived combinatorial formulas for hitting-time moments to the semi-Markov setting. In particular, the mean hitting-time formula coincides with that of a Markov network with the corresponding pseudo-rates, which also yields a short proof of the constancy of Kemeny's constant for finite-mean semi-Markov networks. Finally, we use the same framework to show that weak ergodicity breaking occurs generically for time-additive state observables that are nonconstant on the support of the limiting distribution in heavy-tailed semi-Markov networks.

papers.title: Universality in the target arrival statistics of non-conservative search processes
papers.abstract: Stochastic search processes in which agents are continuously inserted into and removed from a target search domain are fundamental to a wide class of physical and artificial systems. The theory of such non-conservative search processes is, however, much less developed than for search processes with a fixed number of agents. Recent work on the non-conservative case has characterized the fastest first-passage time (FPT) to a target, after which the search process is terminated. Here we consider the complementary problem of continuous arrival statistics to a target. In particular, we derive the full time-dependent distribution of target arrivals, which we use to show that the inter-arrival time distribution is exactly exponential in steady-state regardless of the underlying search process. Thus, counterintuitively, the arrival statistics of non-conservative search are both universal and much simpler than sequential search-and-capture processes involving a fixed number of agents. Our methods also yield an exact expression for the fastest FPT distribution with time-dependent insertion, thereby generalizing previous work on fixed-rate insertion for non-conservative search. Altogether these results have major implications for target resource accumulation, wherein the delivery of resources is counter-balanced by their downstream consumption.

papers.title: Spinodal-controlled freeze-out and nucleation at the first-order superfluid-supersolid transition of a dipolar gas
papers.abstract: Dipolar quantum gases in elongated traps become supersolid through a transition that is continuous at intermediate density but first order at low and high density; at the continuous point, ramps of the scattering length follow Kibble--Zurek scaling. We study ramps across the first-order superfluid--supersolid transition of $^{164}$Dy in an infinite tube using the three-dimensional extended Gross--Pitaevskii equation with truncated-Wigner noise. With quantum noise only, the uniform superfluid survives the metastable window and transforms after its spinodal, where the roton softens. For onsets occurring during the linear ramp, the delay measured from this spinodal has a fitted exponent $\zeta = 0.36 \pm 0.02$, close to the continuous-transition result and the mean-field value $1/3$. The quoted uncertainty combines statistical and systematic sensitivities. Reverse ramps show a comparable delay beyond the fold of the crystal branch, producing dynamical hysteresis. Initial thermal noise with nominal temperatures of 2.5--10 nK produces crystalline regions inside the metastable window during holds, with faster nucleation closer to the spinodal and at higher initial temperature. Without a heat bath these effective rates depend on preparation: ramps crossing the window at the same rate nucleate early in 2 of 32 or 11 of 16 realizations depending on their starting point. A crossover time inferred from hold rates is therefore an estimate, not a measured boundary for the ramp protocol. At low density, slower ramps select larger spacings in a crystal of separated droplets, and droplets survive far above the transition on reverse ramps.

papers.title: Entropy Production in Mesoscopic Electronic Transport Beyond Weak-Coupling
papers.abstract: We investigate the full statistics of entropy production in coherent mesoscopic conductors beyond the weak-coupling regime. Using the inside-outside perspective and the Landauer-B\"uttiker scattering framework, we relate entropy production to the full counting statistics of particle transport and show that the corresponding cumulant-generating function satisfies the fluctuation symmetry independently of the coupling strength. We obtain closed analytical expressions for the cumulant-generating function in the weak- and strong-coupling limits, enabling a detailed characterization of entropy production distributions and higher-order cumulants. These cumulants reveal distinct signatures of resonant transport and coherent fermionic partitioning. While coupling-induced broadening substantially modifies the transport statistics, the fluctuation symmetry imposed by microscopic reversibility remains preserved in the long-time limit.

papers.title: Parametric Glassiness in Graphene-based Electronic L\'evy Glass
papers.abstract: Complex disordered conductors can display highly structured and parameter-sensitive transport even in the absence of a thermodynamically stable glass phase. Overlap distributions originally developed for replica symmetry breaking (RSB) provide a useful diagnostic of this organization, provided that their interpretation is distinguished from the equilibrium Parisi construction. In this study, we report RSB-like overlap phenomenology and parametric mesoscopic glassiness in a graphene-based electronic L\'evy glass, a device that mimics optical phenomena via electronic processes. By tuning the Fermi energy, we can control the number of propagating wave modes and observe reentrant changes from narrowly centered to broad or bimodal overlap distributions. The phenomenology is observed in both graphene-based and conventional two-dimensional electron-gas electronic L\'evy glasses, indicating its generality. Sample-resolved overlap distributions show that the effect is intrinsic to each disorder landscape, whereas the normalized conductance variance shows that the growth of the absolute variance is mainly caused by the increasing mean conductance. We therefore interpret the overlap as a measure of correlation among hierarchically organized transport pathways and the reentrant behavior as evidence of pinning, parameter-induced reorganizations, and mesoscopic chaos in coherent transport.

papers.title: Percolation of Data Constraints and Reorganization of Boolean Function States in Parity Learning
papers.abstract: We study how a neural network reorganizes its learned function as training proceeds and as previously unseen parity data accumulate. The trained model is itself a Boolean function on binary strings of finite length. We then evaluate it on all data, inside and outside the training set, and read off its complete sign table. Its $\pm1$ entries are the amplitudes of a normalized state, dubbed the function-state, whose inverse subsystem purity $K_f=1/\textrm{Tr}(\rho_A^2)$ is an effective Schmidt rank. We find that small data additions broaden the Schmidt spectrum, whereas larger additions reconcentrate it in the target mode. The former is called differentiation because the model distinguishes inputs more sharply. The latter is called target-selective recoherence, where the model settles on the single rule shared by the added data. As the dataset grows, the connectivity of the constraint graph defined by the training set increases monotonically, whereas the learned inverse purity changes nonmonotonically. On a fixed connected dataset, as learning proceeds, the Schmidt spectrum begins to reorganize, followed by gains in target alignment and later by improvement in predictive accuracy. This ordering distinguishes three aspects of learning: constraint identifiability, function-state organization, and predictive accuracy. At fixed data size, a function that has already been learned can re-differentiate, an event we call retreat, without changing graph connectivity. Recovery reconcentrates the Schmidt spectrum in a similar target-selective pattern, without exact recurrence of the Boolean state. Thus the percolation of data constraints fixes the identifiable support, while the reduced state produced by training continues to reorganize even after that support stops changing.

papers.title: Finite-Size Effects in Quantum Metrology at Strong Coupling: Microscopic vs Phenomenological Approaches
papers.abstract: Equilibrium quantum metrology is often formulated under assumptions of weak system-bath coupling and thermodynamic limit scaling, which may not be valid for realistic finite-size (FS) quantum devices. Here, we establish how strong coupling (SC) and FS effects jointly modify achievable precision bounds for equilibrium quantum probes. Considering a transverse-field anisotropic XY spin chain coupled to a thermal environment, first utilize we derive a full polaron transform to derive the effective Hamiltonian at equilibrium. Then, using the bare Hamiltonian and the obtained effective Hamiltonian and taking into account the role of FS effects in the calculation of partition function, we derive an analytic expressions for the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for a general parameter for the equilibrium state in weak coupling (WC) and SC regimes, respectively. In contrast to this microscopic approach, we also utilize the Hill's phenomenological nanothermodynamics to calculate an effective QFI expression at SC. Our results, presented for specific cases of magnetometry and thermometry, reveal that considering FS and SC effects lead to substantial and systematic deviations in QFI, even for moderate system sizes, and that commonly used thermodynamic-limit approximations can significantly misestimate precision. This work also highlights the inadequacy of phenomenological approaches in describing the metrological capability and thermodynamic behavior of systems at SC. Our work establishes a consistent framework for evaluating metrological performance of realistic, finite quantum devices operating beyond the weak-coupling paradigm.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning to Harness Approximation Errors for Long-Time Quantum Simulation
papers.abstract: Accurate digital quantum simulation at long times is limited by the accumulation of errors inherent to approximate simulation. Here we introduce RL-Trotter, a reinforcement-learning framework that treats unavoidable approximation errors as resources for error correction rather than merely imperfections to suppress. We show that low-dimensional information from conservation laws, such as the energy and energy variance, provides a sufficient learning signal to guide the agent, which learns to adapt a single scalar---the next Trotter step size---without access to the target wave function. By optimizing the entire long-time evolution rather than individual steps, RL-Trotter discovers self-correcting sequences in which later errors compensate for those accumulated earlier, increasing the accuracy of the long-time dynamics. The learned policies are intrinsically robust to measurement noise, substantially reducing measurement overhead. They also generalize to previously unseen, physically similar initial states and transfer from small, classically simulable systems to systems an order of magnitude larger. This enables a practical protocol based on classical pretraining followed by direct deployment or limited fine-tuning on quantum hardware. Our results establish a broader perspective for quantum algorithms: errors in approximate evolution can be orchestrated into resources for accurate and resource-efficient quantum dynamics.

papers.title: Quantum Fisher Information of Driven-Dissipative Systems from Keldysh Path Integrals
papers.abstract: Driven-dissipative many-body quantum systems can be exploited in quantum enhanced sensing protocols. Here, non-classical correlations may allow one to reach a measurement precision that surpasses the standard quantum limit. The relevant figure of merit for assessing such quantum advantage is the quantum Fisher information (QFI). In a many-body setting its computation is challenging as it requires knowledge of the full system-environment state. Here we make use of a field-theoretical approach, which is particularly well suited for systems with many degrees of freedom. In particular, we exploit that the QFI can be linked to a Keldysh path-integral. This route leads to a semiclassical expression of the QFI, which is obtained through a controlled expansion in the so-called quantum fields. We benchmark the framework on three systems of increasing complexity: the driven-dissipative harmonic oscillator, the boundary time crystal - which becomes semiclassical at large system sizes - and a two-dimensional array of collectively emitting atoms. We assess in which parameter regimes the semiclassical description holds and gives access to system sizes beyond the reach of exact methods.

papers.title: Classification of topological phases of matter in stochastic systems
papers.abstract: Topological phases of matter support edge states protected from random perturbations, and the identification of the discrete non-spatial symmetries and dimensions that support such phases was systematically developed for quantum systems and analogous platforms. While topological phases were also discovered in stochastic systems and posited as mechanisms for key biochemical processes, a classification consistent with their Markovian constraints remains lacking, impeding generalization to new scenarios. To address this, we develop new methods including a new homotopy approach, real-space invariants and a redefinition of the point gap to classify both transient and steady states. We find robust transient states in two symmetry classes, no symmetry and pseudo-Hermiticity respectively, while topological steady states are expected only in systems without symmetry. We identify the dimensions with non-trivial phases and their group structure, creating a rigorous framework for predicting robust behavior in active and living matter.

papers.title: Entropic-ordered superfluid
papers.abstract: We present a minimal classical lattice model of superfluidity at arbitrarily high temperatures, using a modified three-dimensional XY model with ``soft" rotors. The global U(1) symmetry is spontaneously broken above a positive critical temperature due to entropic order. We study hydrodynamics in this high-temperature regime and verify consistency with the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, explaining how the large noise variance at very high temperatures is not sufficient to destroy superfluidity or the long lifetime of Goldstone modes.

papers.title: Spectral optimization of spherical lattices and applications to classical and quantum interacting spin systems
papers.abstract: We develop an optimization algorithm for spherical lattice discretizations based on the spectrum of the discretized Laplace operator. Starting from refined icosahedral lattices, we minimize the splitting of the $(2\ell+1)$, $\ell=0,1,2,\dots$, continuum multiplets expected from $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ symmetry via gradient descent. This approach simultaneously produces lattices based on triangles with nearly uniform circumradii and perimeters. Although the optimization uses only the free-particle spectrum, we show that the resulting lattices carry over to interacting models. On the optimized lattices, rotational symmetry is restored for the critical Ising and Potts models and primary scaling dimensions are accurately reproduced for the three-dimensional Ising conformal field theory, when appropriate geometry-dependent interaction strengths are used. Higher-angular-momentum descendant states reveal weak residual symmetry breaking beyond the sectors protected by the underlying icosahedral symmetry.

papers.title: Quadratic XY-anisotropy correction to the spontaneous staggered magnetization of the gapped XYZ spin-$1/2$ chain
papers.abstract: The staggered order parameter of the gapped XYZ spin-$1/2$ chain follows from the eight-vertex solution, but in elliptic variables that fix the Hamiltonian couplings only implicitly. We derive a closed form for the coefficient governing the leading quadratic response of the spontaneous staggered magnetization to the XY anisotropy at fixed longitudinal anisotropy in the gapped antiferromagnetic regime. Starting from the Baxter--Kelland--Jimbo--Miwa--Nakayashiki polarization formula, we show that at fixed longitudinal anisotropy both the modular nome and the crossing-parameter variable of the formula move with the XY anisotropy, and that the motion of the crossing-parameter variable reverses the sign of the expansion at fixed elliptic variables. The coefficient is a rational term plus a Lambert series. It is strictly negative and bounded above by a rational function of the longitudinal anisotropy, to which it is asymptotic in the Ising limit. At the isotropic point it diverges as the inverse five-halves power of the distance to that point, and since the Lambert sum has an asymptotic expansion with exponentially small remainder, the subleading terms of the divergence also follow in closed form. When the XY anisotropy vanishes as the five-fourths power of the distance to the isotropic point, the ratio of the perturbed to the unperturbed order parameter tends to a Gaussian in the scaling variable, and the quadratic truncation is controlled when that variable is small. A fourth-order perturbative calculation in the spin chain, with no input from the eight-vertex solution, reproduces the leading strong-coupling behaviour, and infinite-DMRG calculations at four anisotropies in the gapped regime are consistent with the closed form.

papers.title: Altermagnetic Control of Charge-4e Superconductivity
papers.abstract: We present, to our knowledge, the first theoretical realization of an independent charge-4e phase in a two-dimensional classical array of conventional superconductors coupled through altermagnetic junctions. Tuning the altermagnetic splitting suppresses the leading single-pair tunneling harmonic while retaining strong double-pair coupling, producing a finite charge-4e region between staggered and uniform charge-2e states. Using the complete temperature-dependent microscopic Josephson spectrum, we find short-range ordinary pair correlations alongside algebraic coherence of pairs of Cooper pairs. Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless scaling and a half-flux response further identify the charge-4e phase. Our results establish altermagnetism as a microscopic means to select between ordinary and composite superconducting coherence.

papers.title: Utilizing Neural Networks for Solving Functional Renormalization Group Flow Equations
papers.abstract: A novel physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) based approach for solving functional renormalization group flow equations is presented. We investigate the finite temperature phase transition in $O(N)$ models without relying on the large-$N$ approximation, which was used in earlier attempts with similar methods. We argue that these previous solutions cannot easily be generalized for more complex symmetries, and hence our approach can provide new insight. Our technique relies on a series of ans\"atze that combines the small- and large-field approximation schemes with a neural network, leading to a highly accurate approximation over the entire field range. We compare the PINNs approach with traditional grid-based Runge-Kutta results and show that the network can successfully learn the temperature, field, and scale dependencies of the effective potential in the local potential approximation.

papers.title: Replica Transition at Measurement-Altered Ising Criticality
papers.abstract: Performing measurements on gapless quantum ground states can give rise to new universal phenomena, whose origins remain poorly understood even for the paradigmatic Ising critical point. Replica methods offer a natural framework to study such post-measurement ensembles, with the replica limit $Q\to 1$ describing physical Born-averaged observables. Here we show that, for the monitored critical Ising chain, the replicated post-measurement ensemble of states itself undergoes a phase transition precisely at the physically relevant replica limit $Q \to 1$, preventing standard replica treatments. We use boundary conformal field theory (BCFT) methods to explain the underlying mechanism of this transition. Our methods yield a perturbative analytic calculation of the universal $O(1)$ constant in the Shannon entropy of the measurement record, previously known only numerically. We also apply our tools to study measurement-averaged spin correlators, providing a unified description of the universal properties of measurement outcomes and post-measurement states in the critical Ising chain.

papers.title: Robust Golden Ratio universality as a consequence of a circulant symmetry
papers.abstract: We find a robust scenario for the emergence of the Golden Ratio (GR) dynamical universality class, characterized by the dynamical exponent $z \equiv \varphi=\frac{1}{2}(1+\sqrt{5})$. Previously, its emergence required fine-tuning of system parameters. Here, the GR universality class appears generically in a wide class of Markov processes as a consequence of a global, circulant symmetry of the flux Jacobian. This symmetry leads to GR universality in systems where the total number of conservation laws is odd and larger than three. We introduce a multilane exclusion process with Bernoulli stationary measure as a minimal, parameter-free model, which features GR universality for all conserved modes, most of which are doubly degenerate. Our predictions, based on mode-coupling theory generalized to treat degenerate conserved modes, are corroborated by large-scale Monte Carlo simulations.

papers.title: Error correction and quantum information spreading on sparse random graphs
papers.abstract: Quantum error-correcting codes on graph geometries beyond regular euclidean lattices have emerged as a promising route toward robust quantum information processing. A major challenge in quantum error correction is the trade-off between favorable properties of codes constructed in high dimensionality and the need for locality in practical implementations on near-term hardware. Sparse intermediate geometries may combine the advantages of both, but how their structure governs quantum information dynamics and code performance remains unclear. Here we show that the spectral dimension $d_s$, defined from the low-energy spectrum of the graph Laplacian, is the universal parameter connecting these properties. Using Floquet random Clifford circuits on two distinct sparse graph architectures with tunable spectral dimension, we find that $d_s$ governs both quantum information spreading and the scaling of the resulting quantum error-correcting code distance. We identify a geometry-induced entanglement phase transition from localized area-law to ergodic volume-law, whose universality is determined by $d_s$ and exhibits long-range percolation criticality. In the ergodic phase, the circuit acts as a CSS code encoder whose code distance is set by the competition between two logical sectors --- the cost of severing the graph and the length of its shortest winding cycle --- which connectivity pushes in opposite directions. The spectral dimension organizes this trade-off, highlighting a maximum at intermediate $d_s$ retaining sparse connectivity and physical realizability.

papers.title: Dissipative Majorana Chain---Anomalies and Non-Invertible Symmetries
papers.abstract: We study symmetries and anomalies of dissipative Majorana chains described by Lindblad dynamics. Using the operator-state mapping, we represent the Lindbladian as a non-Hermitian operator on a doubled Hilbert space. In this formulation, the ket and bra contours admit strong fermion parities and strong translations, while their diagonal combinations define weak symmetries. For even and odd chain lengths, we diagnose anomalies by comparing symmetry algebras with and without weak fermion-parity defects. These algebras retain the lattice precursor of the modulo-$8$ anomaly of the closed Majorana chain and exhibit projective relations between strong fermion parity and weak translation, as well as between weak fermion parity and strong translation, which are intrinsic to open quantum systems. We establish the IR correspondence between the lattice symmetry algebras and those of the doubled Majorana CFT in four spin sectors, identifying chiral fermion parities emanated from the lattice translations. Finally, we develop the lattice bosonization of the dissipative chain. For even length with collective energy dephasing, combining the defect and no-defect sectors and imposing GSO projections gives rise to an Ising Lindbladian with non-invertible Kramers--Wannier symmetries descending from the anomalous strong translation and fermion parity of the Majorana chain. For odd length, constructing mutually commuting ket- and bra-sector spin operators instead yields an Ising Lindbladian with a Kramers--Wannier duality defect. Our results provide a controlled framework for extending lattice anomalies and non-invertible symmetries to open quantum systems.

papers.title: An Instability of the Quantum Markov Length
papers.abstract: The Markov length, the length scale governing the exponential decay of conditional mutual information (CMI) in a quantum many-body state, has proven useful for characterizing mixed-state phases of matter. Nevertheless, we show that a state's Markov length is not generally stable under weak local channels. The failure of stability occurs already at a pure product state. We demonstrate this explicitly in a one-dimensional fermionic chain, where a fine-tuned depth-two circuit of nearest-neighbor Gaussian channels maps the vacuum to a state whose CMI decays \emph{algebraically} and whose Markov length is therefore infinite, even when the channels are taken arbitrarily close to the identity. The algebraic decay is rooted in the nonanalyticity of the von Neumann entropy at rank-deficient density operators. We exhibit an analogous instability on an ordinary qubit chain. More generally, we show that the Markov length is unstable in any translation-invariant state with even a single rank-deficient reduced density operator. These results pose a challenge to recent definitions of mixed-state phase equivalence based on the Markov length.

papers.title: When irrelevance governs: dissipation-regression scaling in open quantum criticality
papers.abstract: The real-time dynamics of quantum phase transitions in open systems coupled to finite-temperature environments sits at the heart of contemporary condensed-matter and quantum-information science. Here, invoking a Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, we uncover that, within the coherence-dominated regime of critical real-time evolution, a dissipative coupling deemed naively irrelevant determines, counterintuitively, the longest timescale that holds sway. Possessing a well-defined temporal scaling dimension, it engenders a novel dissipation-regression scaling that systematically reproduces the unusual Kibble-Zurek scaling and relaxation observed in recent numerical studies. By contrast, dissipation-dominated dynamics behaves qualitatively differently. There, furthermore, we show that the discretized and diagonalized formulations of the same open quantum Ising chain realize distinct universality classes.

papers.title: Predicting the Final Stationary State of Sheared 2D Euler Fluids
papers.abstract: The Kelvin-Helmholtz (KH) instability is a fundamental signature of the natural world, manifesting in phenomena ranging from atmospheric clouds to the iconic turbulence of Jupiter's Great Red Spot. While the linear dynamics of this instability is well-understood, the ultimate fate of the fluid --- the final stationary state to which it relaxes --- remains a formidable challenge. In this paper, we present a general non-equilibrium statistical mechanics framework that allows us to predict the asymptotic vorticity distribution of a sheared 2D Euler fluid. By constructing a self-consistent ansatz for the solution of the Vlasov equation, we determine the stationary stream function without explicitly solving the time-dependent Euler equations. We demonstrate that the relaxation leads to a population-inverted core, where high-energy states are fully occupied, surrounded by a tenuous halo of vortices in the lower-energy regions of configuration space. This result establishes the core-halo structure as a robust statistical consequence of the system's evolution, offering a universal framework for understanding the saturation of shear-induced turbulence in inviscid 2D fluids.

papers.title: Locality-Preparation Time Tradeoffs in Dissipative Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Dissipative state preparation engineers quantum many-body states as steady states of an open-system dynamics. The spatial range of the required dissipation sets both the feasibility of analog implementations and the connectivity and control complexity of digital ones. Yet how this locality quantitatively constrains preparation times remains largely unknown. Here, we establish an exact locality-preparation time relation for quadratic fermionic systems and develop a construction that optimizes the locality of the dissipative dynamics while preserving the target state. Applied to the Kitaev chain, our framework reveals sharply different locality-preparation time tradeoffs in critical and gapped regimes. At criticality, suppressing the algebraic tails of the jump operators necessarily forces the preparation time to grow algebraically with system size. By contrast, both trivial and topological gapped phases admit exponentially localized dissipation with a finite preparation time in the thermodynamic limit. Our results identify when fast dissipative preparation is compatible with local control and when criticality imposes an unavoidable dynamical cost.

papers.title: A Warped Born Rule Turns an Observer into a Maxwell's Demon
papers.abstract: Quantum mechanics seems to be an incredibly delicate theory. Slight alterations to nearly any part of its structure can lead to huge qualitative differences and wildly unphysical predictions. Here, we explore the many-body consequences of replacing the Born rule $p(m)\propto\|P_m|\psi \rangle|^2$ by a warped rule $p_b(m)\propto\|P_m|\psi\rangle\|^{2b}$. Specifically, in systems with conserved particle number, evolution punctuated by repeated local particle observations acquires a probabilistic bias over measurement histories with an effect controlled by the sign of $b-1$. For $b>1$, this bias generically drives the gas to collect into nearly frozen configurations. Similar to the action of Maxwell's demon, the simple act of observation seems to extract entropy from a closed system. For $b<1$, the bias is reversed, generically scouring out long-wavelength fluctuations to produce a hyperuniform gas. We study this effect in a one-dimensional quantum gas, where these two phases are derived analytically for a particular measurement scheme and corroborated numerically for more general procedures with discrete-time projective-measurement circuit models using matrix product state simulations. We additionally discuss how this bias manifests in a common technique that often employs this warped rule, the ``replica trick,'' implying qualitative differences between finite-replica and replica-limit calculations.

papers.title: Mixed eigenstates in spin-boson systems with one-photon and two-photon interactions
papers.abstract: Spin-boson systems have attracted increasing attention as accessible experimental platforms and for their potential applications in designing quantum technologies. One characteristic of these systems is the transition from regular to completely chaotic behavior when certain control parameters are varied. However, the characterization of their mixed phase space has not been thoroughly explored. In this work, we investigate the properties of mixed eigenstates in spin-boson systems, comparing one-photon interactions with two-photon interactions. We propose a generalized definition of the phase-space overlap index to identify genuine mixed eigenstates. Our study highlights the fundamental differences that arise when two-photon processes are considered compared to one-photon processes and provides complementary evidence supporting the validity of the principle of uniform semiclassical condensation of quasiprobability functions in spin-boson systems.
